rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to capture all 10 compounds, estimate the active elution window, and see whether any peaks are unretained or still in the final hold. The long, wide gradient maximizes information on retention distribution and selectivity for the first iteration.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only gain is to bring the last peak under 10 min. The observed elution window maps to roughly phi_e 0.11 to 0.59, so a trimmed, steeper gradient centered on that window should keep all peaks in-gradient while shortening the run substantially.

Resolution still has comfortable margin, so push for shorter retention by increasing temperature and modestly steepening/raising the high end to accelerate the last peak. This should test whether all 10 can stay fully resolved while moving t_last to about 10 min or below.

The limiting pair lost resolution when temperature and upper phi were pushed, while all peaks are now comfortably before 10 min. Backing off temperature and slightly narrowing the window should recover the 6/7 separation while likely keeping t_last under 10 min.

The critical 6/7 pair is very sensitive to slope and benefits from the hotter selectivity, so keep T at 50 C but make the gradient shallower to recover their resolution. This should still keep the last peak under 10 min while potentially lifting the resolution term toward 1.0.

The critical pair clearly is not improved by shallower slope, so its separation is governed more by where it sits in the phi window than by tG. Shift the whole gradient window lower at 50 C to move peaks 6/7 to a less compressed solvent-strength region while keeping the run short enough to preserve the zero time penalty.

The critical pair worsened when T dropped from 50 to 45 C and also when the phi window was shifted lower, so the best lever appears to be higher temperature near the original successful window. Try 55 C at the same 0.15–0.60, 8 min program to see if selectivity flips further in our favor while retaining the sub-10 min last peak.

At 55 C the former critical 6/7 pair is fixed and only pair 4/5 is slightly below full credit, so a modestly shallower gradient at the same phi window and temperature is the cleanest way to spread that local region. The time margin is large enough that increasing tG from 8 to 10 min should still keep t_last under 10 min while potentially reaching full resolution credit.

A slightly narrower window may preserve full resolution while shortening the late part of the run, potentially giving an equally optimal method with a bit less unnecessary high-organic exposure. This probes whether the 0.60 upper limit is more than needed for the last peak while staying close to the proven optimum.

You already have a max-score method, so this is a neighboring robustness/shortcut test: raising temperature may further shorten the run while keeping all pairs at or above 1.5. If selectivity holds, it could reveal another 1.000-point method with more speed margin; if not, the current optimum remains secured.

The optimum at 55 C is established; this neighboring window tests whether shifting the entire gradient slightly higher preserves full resolution while moving the elution band earlier, which could still keep CRF at 1.000 and identify a more aggressive equivalent method. The 60 C result suggests temperature is too strong a selectivity lever, so keep T at 55 C and vary only the phi window.

The higher-window test compressed both the earliest pair and 4/5, so move in the opposite direction while holding the proven temperature and slope. Lowering phi0 may restore extra space for the front while keeping the successful 55 C selectivity and enough high-end strength for the last peak.

You already have a perfect method; this adjacent test checks whether a slightly higher phi1 can preserve full credit while shortening the tail without raising phi0 enough to compress the front pair. It maps the local optimum around the proven 0.15/0.60/10/55 condition.

With 55 C fixed as the best selectivity, test a slightly shallower slope around the proven window to see whether both marginal pairs gain extra resolution while remaining under the 10 min threshold. This is a robustness check around the exact optimum and may reveal another max-score plateau.

This combines the two one-sided boundary moves that each nearly retained full credit: lower phi0 helped pair 4/5, while lower phi1 slightly favored keeping all pairs resolved with only a tiny time penalty. Testing 0.10–0.55 at 55 C and 10 min maps whether a narrower, lower window can still hit the max-score plateau.

A hotter, steeper run sharply compressed pair 4/5, so this tests whether restoring the steeper 8 min slope at 60 C can trade some of that compression into better local spacing while preserving the very short runtime. It also cleanly separates temperature and slope effects around the 55–60 C optimum region.

At 55 C, increasing phi1 to 0.65 only slightly hurt pair 4/5 at tG 10, so trying the same higher endpoint with the steeper 8 min gradient maps whether slope and window can offset each other and reveal another short, fully resolved method. This explores the remaining nearby corner around the proven optimum without disturbing the successful temperature.

The 55–60 C region mainly trades speed for selectivity losses in pair 4/5, while lower temperature tends to favor that region. This run tests whether a slightly higher phi0 combined with 50 C can keep the last peak under 10 min yet shift selectivity enough to recover full resolution by moving away from the 55 C critical-pair behavior.

This is the key missing control around the optimum: same proven phi window and slope as injection 8, but at 50 C instead of 55 C. It cleanly isolates the temperature effect on the critical pairs and tests whether full resolution might also be achieved at the lower temperature with t_last still under 10 min.

Lower temperature shifts the critical problem back to pair 6/7, so this targeted window shift tests whether placing the band slightly higher while keeping phi1 moderate can improve that pair without sacrificing the sub-10 min last peak. It explores the opposite direction from the lower-phi trials that also hurt 6/7.

The best method is already secured, so use a final broad local probe around it: lowering phi0 helped pair 4/5 while raising phi1 helped time, and each change alone only slightly reduced the score. Combining them tests whether both marginal regions can be balanced simultaneously to uncover another max-score window at 55 C.

Now that 0.10–0.65 at 10 min is also perfect, test whether the same broader 55 C window can be run faster without losing full resolution. This is the most direct attempt to identify a shorter max-score method on the new optimum plateau.

The 8 min version slightly under-resolved pair 4/5, while the 10 min version was perfect with margin; a 12 min run will test how broad the full-resolution plateau is on this second optimum window. This is a robustness check that may show whether 0.10–0.65 remains max-score under shallower conditions.

On the 0.10–0.65 optimum, pair 6/7 is the limiting pair, so lowering phi0 one more step may open late-mid spacing while keeping the strong high end and 55 C selectivity that already delivered a max score. This tests the lower edge of the optimal plateau with two injections left.

The last run suggests lowering phi0 further only slightly under-resolves 6/7, so with one injection left, raise phi1 one step while keeping the successful 55 C and 10 min slope to see if the stronger high end restores that pair without pushing t_last above 10 min. This probes the last nearby unexplored point around the second max-score plateau.
